register.source_checks: The certificate's JSON report states S_input 13.970916436217552 and S_exact 13.97091643621467873524…, the side of a Newton-converged KKT point at 80 digits, and the issue reports that the source's two exact checkers, verify_cert.py and verify_cert2.py, both print VALID; the certificate's header names verify_cert.py, byte-identical to the copy the n183 packet retains. The issue reports a local minimum of the side, strict modulo 43 exact flat motions, from numerical checks at 80 digits that are not interval proofs. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here. From the two sides it states, the certificate's side lies above S_exact by about 1.40e-19, a relative padding of 1e-20.
register.credit: Credit Evan Daniel (https://github.com/evand/square-packing), from an L-cut of Francisco Couzo's 211 packing (T-188), an arrangement of Daniil Ostashev's design (T-175). The issue asks that 'the register's s(211) packing (Daniil Ostashev; also in Francisco Couzo's repository)' be credited as the start; the register's packing at the side the issue gives for it is T-188's, and where T-188 differs from Ostashev's own 211 packing the certificate follows T-188 (M-1 of the 25 October review). Two Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard entries the issue quotes state a side and no packing, so neither is a report: Subramanya N's 13.9709164362306 of 24 October, 1.59e-11 above this side, and Prathamesh Chavan's 13.9727613470647 of 23 October. The source's credits say its work was produced by Claude (Anthropic) under human direction, and the commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer naming Claude.
